units.text: `@GraphicsMode` is a Configurer annotation for controlling which graphics shadow implementation is used for the android.graphics package. Its modes:

quotes.quote: A Configurer annotation for controlling which graphics shadow implementation is used for the android.graphics package.

units.text: - `GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE`: use graphics shadows libraries backed by native Android graphics code.

quotes.quote: Use graphics shadows libraries backed by native Android graphics code.

units.text: - `GraphicsMode.Mode.LEGACY`: use legacy graphics shadows that are no-ops and fakes.

quotes.quote: Use legacy graphics shadows that are no-ops and fakes.

units.text: The Robolectric simulator page's example test class is annotated with `@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)`.

quotes.quote: @GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)

units.text: Robolectric 4.10 added support for native Android graphics. The 4.10 release notes say it can be enabled using `@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)`. When native graphics is enabled, interactions with Android graphics classes use real native Android graphics code and are much higher fidelity.

quotes.quote: can be enabled using @GraphicsMode(NATIVE)
When native graphics is enabled, interactions with Android graphics classes use real native Android graphics code and are much higher fidelity

units.text: The Robolectric blog post "Designing local testing libraries" describes itself as "an outside read of the code as it stands in mid-2026, not an official AndroidX position". In its section on Jetpack Compose UI test, the post says screenshot tests use Robolectric's native-graphics PixelCopy shadow.

units.text: `ComposeTestRule` exposes its test clock as `mainClock`. You can set the `autoAdvance` property to false to control the clock in your test code. After initiating the animation you want to test, the clock can be moved forward with `advanceTimeBy`.
